historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Cholesterol absorption inhibitors

starting.description: In an ACAT-inhibitor program, synthetic azetidinone byproduct 6 and related compounds showed a reproducible cholesterol-lowering effect in cholesterol-fed hamsters despite weak or noncorrelating ACAT inhibition. The team followed that animal effect to create the SCH 48461 absorption-inhibitor prototype.

inspiration.description: Known rodent cholesterol handling initially motivated ACAT testing. The class-opening lead was a synthetic azetidinone's observed hamster lipid effect, followed by observed activity of SCH 48461 metabolites.

steps.description: A planned ACAT-inhibitor program made constrained compounds, including an azetidinone byproduct with weak ACAT activity but an in-vivo lipid effect.

The team optimized the animal effect rather than the enzyme assay and produced the prototype cholesterol absorption inhibitor SCH 48461. A later animal uptake comparison distinguished its effects from an ACAT inhibitor.
Metabolite-bile experiments and synthesis of candidate metabolites informed the development of the more potent second-generation analogue ezetimibe.
Later genetic experiments implicated NPC1L1 in the ezetimibe-sensitive intestinal cholesterol absorption pathway; the protein was not the starting target used to discover the class.

design.description: Medicinal chemists optimized azetidinone analogues against animal activity and designed ezetimibe using favorable metabolite features and strategic fluorine substitutions to block unfavorable metabolic sites.

circumstances.description: The ACAT program and subsequent analogue optimization were planned; the useful lipid effect of a weak-ACAT reaction byproduct and the assay disconnect supplied the serendipitous turn.

limits: This record covers the azetidinone lineage represented by ezetimibe, not statins or every possible inhibitor of intestinal sterol absorption. S2 also names tiqueside as a cholesterol absorption inhibitor approach; its founding history and membership were not evaluated (E11).
conflicts: A 2022 secondary review (S6, E10) calls SCH 58235 itself a metabolite of SCH 48461 and attributes the metabolite-bile comparison to it. The S3 abstract (E7) instead compares parent with metabolite-containing bile and identifies a C4-phenol glucuronide as the most active fraction; the S2 original (E5-E6) describes the design of SCH 58235 from a putative-metabolite structure-activity analysis. The record follows those primary accounts for the narrower designed-analogue description, while noting S3 full text was not read.
gaps: The initial compound-6 original, Burnett et al. 1994 (S7), was located but not read, and PubMed has no abstract; the founding chronology rests on the discoverer retrospective S1. Full 1995, 1997, and 2004 primary reports were not read, and those reports are represented at abstract extent, with the 1995 abstract truncated.
